# MIDIMaster

Editors and librarians for MIDI synthesizers and effects units that run in the browser and work
entirely over MIDI. Each editor is mapped from the device's own firmware, so parameters, ranges and
value texts read as they do on the device's display.

## Desktop app (Windows, macOS, Linux)

The desktop app needs no browser or server: install it and start it. It is the same app, with Web MIDI
and SysEx allowed for its own pages only.

| System | Download |
|---|---|
| Windows | `MIDIMaster-Setup-<version>-x64.exe` (installer; arm64 too) or `MIDIMaster-<version>-portable.exe` (runs without installing) |
| macOS | `MIDIMaster-<version>-universal.dmg` (Intel and Apple silicon) |
| Linux | `MIDIMaster-<version>.AppImage` (runs without installing) or the `.deb` package |

The builds are not code-signed yet. Windows SmartScreen asks once ("More info", then "Run anyway").
On macOS, open the app with right-click, Open, the first time.

## Browser version

- **Browser:** Chrome or Edge on a desktop computer (Web MIDI with SysEx). Firefox and Safari are not
  supported.
- **Server:** Node.js 20 or later. If Node is not installed, `start.bat` falls back to Python 3's
  built-in server.

1. Double-click `start.bat` (Windows), or run `node serve.js` and open `http://localhost:8020/`.
   The page must come from `localhost` (or HTTPS): browsers only allow SysEx there.
2. Allow MIDI access with SysEx when the browser asks.

## First steps

- **MIDI:** connect a MIDI interface or the device's USB MIDI port both ways (out to the device's In,
  the device's Out to in).
- **Find your devices:** press **Scan MIDI ports** on the front page. It asks every port which device
  is on it and lists what it finds under Connected. A device found there opens on its ports.
- **Or pick a device** from the list and choose its ports, channel and device ID on its Connect page.
- **Demo mode:** add `?demo` to the address (`http://localhost:8020/?demo`) to try any editor without
  hardware.

## Building

- **Tests:** `node --test tests/`. The app itself has no build step and no dependencies.
- **Desktop app from source:** `npm install`, then `npm run app` to start it, or `npm run dist:win`,
  `dist:mac`, `dist:linux` to build installers into `dist/`. macOS builds need a Mac; the
  `Desktop builds` GitHub workflow builds all three on a version tag.

## What it does

- **Editor pages for each device:** patches, performances, multis and system settings. Every change is
  sent live, and memory banks can be browsed, read, stored and recalled.
- **MIDI channels:** a page for multitimbral devices showing parts, patches and channels.
- **Branch Library (one per device):**
  - complete dumps, recorded dumps, and .syx / .mid imports, each bank as its own entry;
  - send back the whole entry or a selection.
- **Head Library:** one patch store for all devices. Patches can be loaded into another model
  through its translator.
- **MIDI inputs:** up to four controllers, with controller mappings (e.g. CC 1 to filter cutoff). Set
  them once for all devices in Settings, and override them per device.
- **Also:** a controllers page, an audition keyboard, a SysEx console and a MIDI monitor.

## Good to know

- **Saving:** live edits go into the device's edit buffer; storing to memory always asks first.
  Make a complete dump in the Branch Library before experimenting.
- **Memory Protect:** turn it off on the device if it has one, or stores are refused.
- **Long dumps:** complete dumps run in the background. They go on while you use other pages of
  the device and save themselves when done. Leaving the device asks first.
- **USB or DIN:** some devices offer things only over USB or a control port (e.g. the SYSTEM-8's
  CTRL port). The editor disables what the current connection cannot do and says why.
- **Speed:** "Measure speed" on the Connect page finds the fastest pace the device takes on the
  current port. USB is often much faster than DIN MIDI. Each port keeps its own measurement.
- **Where your data is kept:** settings, libraries and measurements are stored in this browser
  profile. Export entries (.syx) to keep them elsewhere.

### Planned next

- **Editors in progress to complete:** the rest of the Yamaha DX family (TX7, DX9, DX5, TX816, DX7II,

### Waiting for firmware or a ROM dump (659)

These will be implemented once their firmware is found: an official update file, an OS disk, or a dump of the ROM chips. If you have one, it helps. (Pianos, organs and home or arranger keyboards are left out of both lists for now.)

## Project layout

```
index.html, css/        the page and its styles (css/theme.css: the Web Awesome theme; css/app.css: the app's own)
vendor/                 bundled libraries, no CDN: Web Awesome (components and styles), Font Awesome Free
                        icons, the Inter font; versions and licenses in vendor/README.md
js/core/                MIDI (Web MIDI, request queue, SysEx), UI parts, libraries, settings
js/shell/               the app: front page, settings, monitor, Head Library
js/devices/             device registry, families, levels; defs/ = one definition per device;
                        generic/ = the editor, library and dump pages every definition uses
electron/               the desktop app (Electron main process); build/ holds its icon
tests/                  node --test suite
tools/                  firmware analysis and table generators per maker
docs/devices/           notes per device: messages, firmware evidence, what was checked
```
